mission: Cockpit. Veraine's comm signal arrives — clean, encrypted in a Sith-era protocol only Kael fully recognises: 'I would prefer to speak rather than be spoken about. I suspect you would as well.' The group debates. Ben keys acceptance before the debate can reopen. Meeting location set between their position and Veranthos.
why_now: Veraine has been invisible for fifteen chapters. She steps forward now because the amplification work needs a moment when the group's attention is elsewhere, and the clean signal is the shape of her timing.
conflict: Desh's tactical read is the one Ben trusts; Sera's archive memory is the one Ben listens to; Torin is for; Kael is silent, which is its own answer. The trap is inside whichever position they choose, and Ben needs intelligence more than he needs certainty.
turning_point: Ben keys the acceptance into the comm and transmits before the debate can reopen. The choice is ratified by action before the group has agreed.
opening_hook: The comm signal is clean, polite, and uses Kael's name. 'I would prefer to speak rather than be spoken about. I suspect you would as well.'
closing_hook: The meeting location: a neutral point between their position and Veranthos. Veraine's ship is already there. One vessel, minimal crew. Either she's supremely confident or supremely prepared. Probably both.
emotional_trajectory: Sharp alarm at contact -> heated debate -> calculated acceptance

stakes.personal: Ben choosing to face the primary antagonist directly
stakes.interpersonal: The group's working trust tested — Ben overriding objections
stakes.external: Veraine has four objectives for this meeting; Ben knows about zero of them

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit, comm active
sensory_details: Veraine's voice across the comm — calm, precise, academic; the protocol's era signature catching Kael's attention before it catches anyone else's; Desh running counter-intelligence scenarios in small fast hand-work on his datapad; Sera's jaw muscles working but no sentence emerging
action_beats: Veraine's comm signal cuts through the cockpit speakers — clean, encrypted in a Sith-era protocol Kael recognizes
Desh runs counter-intelligence scenarios on his datapad while the group debates the truce offer
Ben keys the acceptance into the comm and transmits before the debate can reopen
notes: H10 resolves — Veraine has been leading them so she could have an audience. Her four objectives (pitch, recruit Kael, sabotage cover, intelligence) are not yet visible to Ben, and the scene should not name them from his side. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, list Veraine's possible objectives as interiority. He keys acceptance and the scene moves. Voice: Zahn-procedural, clipped cockpit dialogue, Sera's sentences in her full archaic register under stress. Anti-pattern: do not let any character articulate the four-objective frame on-page; that architecture is for the scene card, not the prose.
